transcript.content: Hello, please have a seat. What brings you into the clinic today?

I, um... I guess I just haven't been doing much lately. Things that usually make me feel like myself, like taking my camera out for walks or mentoring the kids in the neighborhood... even just keeping my calendar organized for work. It all just started feeling really flat. Heavy, I guess. So I just stopped doing them.
About how long have you been feeling this flat and heavy feeling?

It's... it's been a while, I suppose. Maybe a year and three months? Give or take. It started back when, um... well, a family member's health started declining. Their behavior changed a lot, too. I had to step in, take on a lot more of the coordination and just... handling things. It's been like this since then.
Have you ever had periods where you felt the complete opposite—unusually energized, wired, or needing very little sleep for days at a time?

I suppose... occasionally. There have been nights where I only sleep, maybe, two or three hours. I'll wake up before dawn and... I don't really feel tired. I just get up and start answering emails or updating appointment lists for the office. I don't know if I'd call it wired, exactly, but... yeah. I just work.
When those times happen, how many days in a row does that reduced need for sleep usually last?
I don't really know. Maybe... a few days? I don't keep track of it. It just happens sometimes and then it stops.
During those times when you slept so little, how would you describe your mood?

I guess... sometimes I feel pretty good. Like, unusually upbeat, I suppose. Everything just seems to click at work. But then... well, if something small changes, like a meeting gets moved, I can get... sharp with people. It surprises me a bit. But that's about it.
